alerts.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 1 at 7:52PM MST until November 2 at 12:00PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected above 10000 feet. Total snow
accumulations between 12 and 18 inches, with locally higher amounts
possible. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Northwest San Juan Mountains and Southwest San Juan
Mountains.

* WHEN...Until noon MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning commute.

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 4:08PM MST until November 2 at 4:15PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
Significant and historic flooding is occurring across southwest
Colorado and southeast Utah. Widespread rainfall will continue
through Monday. Excessive runoff will also increase flooding risks.
Many local roads have become flooded and impassable. Some roads have
washed out, or collapsed completely. If you live in the warned area,
it is recommended to not travel this evening or overnight. This is a
PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION.

* WHAT...Major flooding caused by excessive rainfall will continue.
This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION.

* WHERE...Western Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...
Western Dolores County in southwestern Colorado...
Southeastern La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...
Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...
West Central San Miguel County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 415 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring. Numerous roads remain
closed due to flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 359 PM MST, local law enforcement reported heavy rain in the
warned area. Flooding is already occurring. Between 1.5 and 3
inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Durango, Blanding, Mexican Hat, Cortez, Pagosa Springs, Dolores,
Dove Creek, Ignacio, Aneth, Montezuma Creek, White Mesa, Bluff,
Tselakai Dezza, Halchita, Goulding, Hovenweep National Monument,
Towaoc, Arriola, Yellow Jacket and Lewis.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.areaDesc: Archuleta, CO; Dolores, CO; La Plata, CO; Montezuma, CO; San Miguel, CO; San Juan, UT

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 10:50AM MST until November 2 at 7:00PM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
...The National Weather Service in Grand Junction CO has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Colorado...

Mancos River near Mancos affecting Montezuma County.

For the Mancos River...including Mancos...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Mancos River near Mancos.

* WHEN...From this evening to Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, Minor flooding can be expected around
Mancos.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 AM MST Sunday the stage was 4.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
evening to a crest of 6.3 feet late this evening. It will then
fall below flood stage late tonight.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 5.7
feet on 05/21/2005.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 10:37PM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and southeast
Utah, including the following areas, Canyonlands/Natural Bridges,
La Sal and Abajo Mountains and Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...From 5 AM MST Sunday through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recently burned areas, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 3 inches of rain is expected across portions of southeast
Utah and southwest Colorado from Sunday morning through Monday
morning over soils that are still saturated from recent rainfall
and flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

alerts.headline: Avalanche Advisory issued October 31 at 7:16PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
alerts.description:
SABCO

THE FOLLOWING MESSAGE IS TRANSMITTED AT THE REQUEST OF THE
COLORADO AVALANCHE INFORMATION CENTER.

...A SPECIAL AVALANCHE ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 4:30 PM SATURDAY
UNTIL 4:30 PM MONDAY...

*WHAT...Avalanche conditions are dangerous above treeline.
*WHERE...West Elk Mountains, Elk Mountains, San Juan Mountains, and
La Plata Mountains
*WHEN...From 4:30 PM Saturday until 4:30 PM Monday.
*IMPACTS...Backcountry travelers can easily trigger dangerous
avalanches large enough to bury a human.

*PRECAUTION/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...A potent winter storm increases
avalanche danger Sunday into Monday. Rain, snow, and wind will cause
natural avalanches above treeline. Check the forecast at
www.colorado.gov/avalanche.

Beyer & Pritchett
